page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-64-lssd is an Arm-based general purpose instance powered by 64 dedicated arm64 vCPUs. The platform provides 256 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual core. It does not include dedicated GPU acceleration, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provided with the standard allocation.

A key physical characteristic of this configuration is the integration of 5637 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage spread across 14 drives. This non-volatile local disk setup provides direct, low-latency access for data-heavy operations, bypassing network latency associated with standard attached cloud block storage.

The combination of 64 dedicated Arm cores, balanced memory density, and extensive local NVMe storage delivers high resource density. This hardware profile eliminates external storage bottlenecks for throughput-sensitive tasks. The instance is suitable for distributed NoSQL and relational databases, high-throughput caching tiers, extract-transform-load (ETL) processing, and search indexing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-64-lssd is a general purpose instance built on the arm64 architecture. It provides 64 dedicated vCPUs alongside 256 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. A key characteristic of the instance is the inclusion of 5637 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage across 14 drives, delivering high-throughput and low-latency disk access for temporary or replicated datasets. The configuration does not include discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By leveraging power-efficient Arm processors and dense local storage, the instance yields a balanced compute and I/O environment without requiring dedicated network-attached block devices. This profile is suited for high-throughput transactional databases, distributed data processing, ETL pipelines, caching layers, and search clusters.
